applicableAreas: All proposed structures within potential clearance distance of overhead electric facilities
findings.comment: Building elevation sheets with surveyed overhead conductor elevations and clearance dimensions are not provided. Plans show proposed buildings (Buildings 1-8) and overhead electric lines running along property boundaries, but no building elevation views showing measured clearances from outside conductor to building faces are included. Cannot verify that required clearances are met without surveyed conductor elevation data.

applicableAreas: All proposed structures and building projections
findings.comment: Section and plan view exhibits showing dimension lines from outer electric conductor to outermost edge of buildings and projections are not provided. Site plan shows building footprints and overhead line locations, but no dimensioned clearance views demonstrating compliance with 7.5-foot sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearance requirements.

applicableAreas: Retaining walls on southern property boundary adjacent to overhead electric distribution line
findings.comment: Retaining wall clearance dimensions from overhead electric conductors are not shown. Site plan indicates concrete retaining walls run along the southern property boundary immediately adjacent to the overhead electric distribution line (---OHE---). Wall plan sheets provide structural section details but do not show clearance dimensions from the outside conductor to the outermost face of the wall. Cannot verify 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance requirement is met.

applicableAreas: Retaining wall section views on southern boundary
findings.comment: Retaining wall section exhibits do not show dimensions from outer electric conductor to wall faces. Wall sections provided show structural reinforcement details and footing design but do not include overhead electric line elevations or clearance dimensions. Cannot verify compliance with clearance requirements from available evidence.

applicableAreas: Driveway entrances on western boundary crossing under overhead electric lines
findings.comment: Driveway vertical clearance dimensions from overhead electric facilities are not shown. Site plan indicates proposed driveway entrances cross under overhead electric lines on the western boundary, but no grading plan section views or clearance calculations are provided to verify minimum 16-foot vertical clearance (without truck traffic) or 18-foot clearance (with truck traffic) is maintained from lowest point of overhead facilities to finished driveway grade.

applicableAreas: All clearance dimension annotations throughout site plan
findings.comment: Site plan shows overhead electric lines but provides no clearance dimension annotations. When clearance dimensions are visible on plans, they must extend from the outside conductor (actual electric wire), not from the utility pole centerline. However, no clearance dimensions are annotated at all on the site plans, preventing verification that dimensions (if any) are measured from the correct point.

applicableAreas: Southern boundary of site under overhead electric distribution line (OHE)
findings.comment: Landscape plan shows proposed mitigation trees (marked with 'M') planted directly under and within 10 lateral feet of the overhead electric distribution line (---OHE---) running along the southern property boundary. Tree species are not identified on the landscape plan and cannot be verified against the Utility Compatible Shade Trees list in ECM Appendix F. According to UCM § 1.10.10.4, trees within 50 lateral feet of transmission lines or within 10 lateral feet of distribution lines must be utility-compatible species with mature height ≤20 feet, or have documented alternative mitigation. No such documentation is provided.

Site Plan Release Notes do not include the required note that owner/contractor must notify Austin Energy at least 48 hours before work begins near high-voltage overhead lines. Plans show overhead electric distribution lines adjacent to the property, and construction will occur nearby, triggering this notification requirement per Texas Health & Safety Code Chapter 752, Section 752.003.
